stories.title: S&P 500 sales growth hits its highest level in nearly five years
stories.summary: S&P 500 companies are posting their fastest revenue growth in almost five years, according to MarketWatch, and CNBC flags the trend as one of the key things to watch in stocks this week. The pickup comes as the current earnings season rolls on and investors look for signs the strength can continue.
stories.whyItMatters: Revenue growth underpins earnings estimates and helps justify elevated valuations, so a genuine acceleration matters more than one driven by cost-cutting alone.
whatToWatch: Whether the sales growth pace holds as more companies report
How this theme factors into the broader market narrative for the week ahead
questions: What is driving the surge — pricing power, volume growth, or one-off items?
Is the growth broad-based across sectors or concentrated in a few?

stories.title: European stocks steady as investors weigh Strait of Hormuz risk
stories.summary: European equities were little changed as traders balanced concerns about risks around the Strait of Hormuz against an upcoming slate of economic data, per Investing.com. The market appears to be in a holding pattern pending clearer signals on both fronts.
stories.whyItMatters: Any disruption to shipping through Hormuz threatens global oil flows, which can quickly feed into inflation expectations and rate-path bets that move equities.

Upcoming U.S. and European data releases

stories.title: FTSE 100 slips as Mideast tensions and reported Iran blockade weigh
stories.summary: London's FTSE 100 fell as investors focused on escalating Middle East tensions and reports of an Iran-linked blockade, according to Investing.com. The move mirrors broader caution across European markets tied to the same regional risks.
stories.whyItMatters: Rising Middle East tension is a classic trigger for higher oil prices and risk-off moves in equities, making it a key variable for portfolios right now.
whatToWatch: Further news on the reported Iran blockade
Oil price reaction to the situation
questions: What exactly does the reported blockade involve?

stories.title: U.S. stock futures flat as traders await inflation data amid fresh Iran uncertainty
stories.summary: U.S. stock index futures held roughly flat as investors braced for upcoming inflation data while also monitoring renewed uncertainty tied to Iran, according to MarketWatch. The combination is keeping markets in a wait-and-see mode.
stories.whyItMatters: Inflation data is a key input for Fed rate expectations, while geopolitical risk around Iran can quickly move oil prices and risk sentiment together.
whatToWatch: The upcoming inflation data release
Any escalation in the Iran-related situation
questions: Which inflation report is due, and when exactly?
How much of a risk premium is already priced into markets?

stories.title: Stocks beating the S&P 500 hit a 4-year high — and may keep climbing
stories.summary: The number of individual stocks outperforming the S&P 500 index is at its highest level in four years, MarketWatch reports, a sign that market gains are broadening beyond the largest names.
stories.whyItMatters: Wider market breadth is generally seen as a healthier signal than gains concentrated in a handful of mega-cap stocks, and it can change how investors think about diversification.
whatToWatch: Whether breadth continues to widen as earnings season progresses
Any pullback in mega-cap leadership that could accompany the shift
questions: What's driving the broadening — rotation out of megacaps or genuine economic strength?
Which sectors are leading the outperformance?

stories.whyItMatters: The return to profitability is a milestone after years of losses tied to Rakuten's heavy investment in building out its mobile business.

stories.title: Australian rare earth miner jumps as much as 29% after U.S. Department of War investment
stories.summary: Shares of an Australian rare earth miner surged as much as 29% after the company received an investment from the U.S. Department of War, CNBC reports.
stories.whyItMatters: The move underscores Washington's push to lock down critical minerals supply chains outside China, a theme that has driven sharp swings in rare earth stocks.
whatToWatch: Whether the stock holds onto its gains
Further U.S. government investment in critical minerals suppliers
questions: Which company received the investment, and how large is it?
What will the funds specifically be used for?
